#1242. Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick

Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

That is how far United have, once again, fallen. Fans in the Stretford End unfurled their “Standards” banner, bearing the faces of Eric Cantona, Roy Keane and Bryan Robson.

It was first revealed in December 2021 in Carrick’s final match as interim following Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s sacking. This should be his final game again, under different, more traumatic, circumstances.

If it is, he is going out having made a stand. He dropped Bruno Fernandes for his outspoken comments, aimed directly at Carrick and his tactics, following the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat away to Como on Wednesday.

At 2-0 down here it was telling that Carrick turned to Matheus Cunha when he substituted Youri Tielemans, who had been so terribly slow and ineffective, at half-time. Carrick did not bring on Fernandes. And he did not turn to the captain after, as he made four substitutions, including bringing on 19-year-old Shea Lacey. That said it all.

The television cameras catching Omar Berrada, the United chief executive, shaking his head in the stands as Carrick’s team gave away goals also told its own story. They have two wins from 12 in all competitions and none in eight. They have only beaten newly promoted Ipswich Town, in August, and Azerbaijan minnows Sabah this season. United were so careless it looked like they could not care less.

There was no guarantee, after Como, that Carrick would remain in charge after this game. So, losing and losing so embarrassingly – it was three, it should have been five – has to have obvious consequences. However cherished Carrick is. However much the fans excuse him. Yes, he has not been helped enough, but he has also not been good enough.

Finishing third and qualifying for the Champions League last season has proved to be the kind of bounce a new manager can achieve, after the pressure was relieved by the sacking of Ruben Amorim, rather than something more sustainable. There was always the fear that Carrick, despite his playing pedigree, might be out of his depth in this job. And so it is proving to be. Especially as he has been hung out to dry. Carrick certainly appeared resigned to his fate.

But what is he coaching? What is he trying to do with United? How does he want his team to play? Yes, there are limitations, but they are badly set up, tactically poor, and struggle to build attacks. The players are not responding, but it does not mean Carrick is blameless.

Bournemouth were not just collectively and individually better – and despite how good they are, that is some indictment of United – but better organised. They knew what they were doing, believed in it and relished it as they collected a fourth victory, and a fourth clean sheet in a row, after a slow start under Marco Rose, the new head coach. It was no shock.

The nature of the goals spoke volumes. For the first, a free-kick was needlessly conceded by Ayden Heaven, who endured a particularly difficult game, as he lunged in recklessly, forcing Evanilson to jump out of the way or risk injury.

Justin Kluivert whipped the ball in beyond the far post and it was met by Rayan, who volleyed in low and precise. The Brazilian was unmarked. Carrick protested – at what? – and the Bournemouth supporters sang “you’re getting sacked in the morning”.

What a finish from Rayan to give Bournemouth the lead! 🔥 https://t.co/9BV0G5Tqgi

The outstanding Rayan should have had a hat-trick but failed to take two chances in the second half, when he only had goalkeeper Senne Lammens to beat, after Bournemouth had already doubled their lead. It came as Leny Yoro slipped over and presented the ball straight to Adrien Truffert, who squared it for Marcus Tavernier to side-foot home. It was that ridiculously easy.

The third was the same, with Evanilson chasing down a ball forward by Tyler Adams. The striker should not have got there. But Harry Maguire, captain in Fernandes’s absence, gave up, pointing at Lammens to win it. Instead, the goalkeeper was beaten to the ball and Evanilson’s finish from an angle, arcing high into the net, was superb.

"What a finish!" 😮‍💨 Evanilson makes it 3-0 to Bournemouth with a stunning goal https://t.co/hPMR78Z3cX

“You’re going down with the City,” goaded the Bournemouth fans and it is that end of the table United need to fret about. Which means, for Carrick, it has to be over. The Stretford End sang his name. But it was out of support for him as a player, his reputation, what he represented, not what is happening now as they once again vented their anger at the owners, director of football, Jason Wilcox, and even the plans for a new stadium.

It was the same as Carrick walked down the tunnel, thumping his chest as his name was sung. Then it turned. The vitriol, frustration and anger dripped down on the players, washing them away.

This felt like a new nadir. And the need for yet another new start away to Chelsea on Saturday.

Former Tottenham defender speaking to the BBC:

Manchester United’s players were just standing there today. I did not see in their body language that they are prepared to do everything for the manager, the club or the fans to change their situation.

It’s an easy thing to say they are lacking leaders but it’s true. They just don’t have big characters. It is not something technical but if you are in a tunnel and you saw the likes of [former Man Utd defenders] Nemanja Vidic or Rio Ferdinand their body language told the opposition that they were going to have a tough afternoon.

Carrick admits he does not know if he will remain in place.

The club have a week off now, with the next match a trip to Stamford Bridge against a tasty Chelsea side, albeit one who lost to Spurs last night.

He says: “It’s a tough situation. What is next? I don’t know. I’ll always do what’s best for this football club. I don’t change that now. I love what I do. I love the responsibility. But we’ll have to wait and see.”

Carrick gives a non-answer over his choice to leave Fernandes on the bench.

He says: “There’s always times when you’re trying to make decisions that are to change the course of play and made a difference but those are the decisions we made today.”

Carrick then denies that his acknowledgement of the crowd was to say goodbye, adding: “It wasn’t a farewell from me. I’m mixed emotions, I’m feeling it for my players, they’re going through a tough spell.

“Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment. Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way.”

Carrick also tells Sky: “It’s really difficult to have a day like this at this football club and feel the emotion and dynamics of what it was like today.

“Not for me personally but for Manchester United. It was really mixed. I feel responsibility with the position I’m in. I’ve been at the club a long time. It hurts a lot going through this.”

Carrick potentially acknowledges that his time is up, telling Sky: “It was a strange, mixed of emotions at the end of the game. It wasn’t a nice way to end the game.

“It was a tough day for the players. We went into the game having been rocked. You can feel that. They’re really hurting and disappointed in there. It’s not a nice feeling. You have to accept it, we’re in that situation.”

Today’s United captain Harry Maguire tells Sky Sports: “It wasn’t good enough. Disappointed to give a goal away so early - another set play - and conceding first in the Premier League it makes it difficult.

“A mistake for the second makes it hard for ourselves. We didn’t perform well enough as individuals or as a team and we didn’t deserve anything from the game.

“It’s not clicking at the moment. Results are not good enough and performances in the last week not good enough. Still early in the season.

“Got to find something, question yourself, look in the mirror - that’s the most important thing - think what you can do more and what more you can contribute to the team and if we do that we’ll get somewhere.”

United players have said this for some time now. Each season they look in the mirror, and each season the supporters get the same.

Telegraph columnist Jamie Carragher thinks Carrick has had enough after that.

His emotional exit after the match suggested as much, with the former Liverpool player telling Sky: “He wants to be put out of his misery tonight.”

The fact that a mid-table team can come to Old Trafford and leave with three points is no longer a surprise.

If anything, it’s unusual when competent teams struggle against United these days.

Quite how replacing a manager changes a decade of falling short solves things, who knows?

At least the scoreline is not a surprise. Bournemouth always tend to win 3-0 at Old Trafford these days

Arne Slot underwhelmed last season, and Liverpool moved swiftly to appoint Andoni Iraola from Bournemouth.

They have defeated an impressive Brighton side 2-0 today, and you can read our report here.

Former Manchester United winger Ashley Young is scathing about the players who have succeeded him.

He told Sky Sports: “Unfortunately for Michael Carrick, it’s so disappointing. The fans are behind him and backing him and of course they are, because he’s a legend of the football club.

“But the players on the pitch showed nothing. They didn’t run, they didn’t look like a team together.

“If you looked at the difference to the Bournemouth team, you’d swap every single player for that Manchester United team. It was a poor showing.”

Extraordinary scenes at the end here. Carrick walks around the pitch waving at the fans and being applauded back. It felt very much like a manager saying goodbye. As he reached the Stretford End they start singing his song and Carrick responds by banging his chest in front of them. But as soon as the manager disappeared down the tunnel the fans instantly turned on the players trailing behind. A crescendo of sustained boos reverberate around as they target the players and make their feelings quite clear.

Picking Fernandes on the bench meant that Carrick got to snub him, but it also means that Sky get to make a point of his efforts to express himself, which does not really help the situation.

The away side now match Manchester City and Liverpool.

3 - This is the third time that Bournemouth gone 3-0 up in a Premier League game at Old Trafford (also in December 2023 and December 2024). Only Liverpool and Man City have done so as many times in the competition (3). Dreamers. https://t.co/6EO4byrwCw

United started poorly, got worse, and the less said about the rest, the better.

Two wins, the last against Sabah in the Champions League, and the other against Ipswich Town.

It’s damning. As Fernandes goes down the tunnel, there are hints of jeers for him from the crowd, too.

The camera cuts to Jason Wilcox in the stands, and Neville observes the decision to sack Carrick, which is likely in the post, will “disgust” fans.

After that win, United are in the bottom six.

Manchester United are soundly beaten for the second time in a week.

Como were hugely impressive in the Champions League. Bournemouth were effective but not special. United managed to regress in short order.

Boos ring out, but the crowd then go back to chanting Carrick’s name. They blame someone else for the troubles.

Neville ponders why United did not buy a left-back, with Dalot playing there once again. He has actually been fairly competent today. The midfielders - who were bought this summer - were probably the least impressive. Andrey Santos and Tielemans have been poor.

Carrick will probably get a decent reception, because most of the venom has been aimed at the owners rather than the head coach.

Jason Wilcox is getting some charming chants about him too, now, and he has shaped a poor squad, going by results.

Five minutes are indicated for the rest of the match. Bournemouth look likelier to get a fourth than United are for a first.

Diakite comes on for the last 30 seconds of normal time, after Smith had dawdled. The United fans are starting to leave in greater numbers now, into the rain.

Kroupi comes on, Smith, Tavernier and Evanilson off. Adli is on, but Diakite is yet to replace Smith, who took too long to come off.

Santos strains to reach a Lacey cross, stood up well to the back post, and wins a corner.

Bournemouth struggle to clear it quickly, but United can’t force a chance.

Bournemouth are sitting back, confident of the three points. United have shown so little today they can hardly be worried.

Lacey is coming on now. Still no Fernandes. Carrick clearly prepared to go down sending a message.

Gary Neville says the situation has turned, “sour,” decrying the summer failure not to buy better midfielders.

Lacey comes on for Amad, who has been very quiet. So no Fernandes.

United are reduced to shooting from distance against the legs of Bournemouth defenders.

Carrick was waiting to bring on Zirkzee has Bournemouth scored their third. Even as United sink to a new low, the United manager seems to be making a point by not bringing on Fernandes. Ratcliffe and the Glazers both being targeted.

Christie on for Cook, and Zirkzee for Baleba.

A long ball holds the ball up as the keeper rushes to intercept. He’s stuck, and Evanilson takes the ball around him, and from a tight angle, outside the box, whips it into an empty net.

"What a finish!" 😮‍💨 Evanilson makes it 3-0 to Bournemouth with a stunning goal https://t.co/hPMR78Z3cX

Joshua Zirkzee is likely to come on in a few seconds. He scored against Como and has looked a little more effective this season than last.

Martinez is penalised for tugging at Rayan.. It might be that Heaven and Martinez are just both having a hard time against an exceptional player.

Rayan has been humiliating United all afternoon and should have scored again there after darting away easily from Dalot, who tries to pull him back, and then breezes past Martinez who just falls to the ground. His shot dragged wide of the far post. Great from the Bournemouth winger, risible from United.

Martinez is skinned by Rayan after he beat Dalot, with Baleba struggling, and he shoots a fraction wide.

Heaven was really off the pace today, and that is a worry for a player who had such promise.

Evanilson needs some treatment after being caught accidentally by Santos as they challenged for a high ball.

Our first change here 🔄 https://t.co/DgHNkHmxn3

Dalot’s run down the left wing earns him a corner.

Mount will take, but Petrovic claims under little pressure.

Andrey Santos goes down in the box but the ref is in no mood.

United come again, Dalot crossing into the box, but it’s headed away.

The ball comes back to Mbeumo, and his shot from the right-hand side of the box is too high.

6 - For only the sixth time, Bruno Fernandes has been named on the bench for a Premier League game. Today is the first time Michael Carrick has named a Premier League starting XI without Fernandes in it. Omitted. https://t.co/96pxeW8qed

Fernandes starts warming up, bringing a small round of applause, rather than a roar.

“Carrick needs goals,” Neville correctly observes.

Benjamin Sesko has been a big miss, as the Slovenian had been improving under Carrick, but Mbeumo and Cunha had looked lively last season.

Cunha misses from the edge of the box, attempting to curl one into the top corner with his left foot.

The crowd are getting restless now. United are drifting.

United look totally and utterly shot. The first five minutes of the second half have been shocking and Bournemouth could be three or four ahead.

Heaven blasts the ball into an opponent, Maguire miscontrols it, and the ball is worked to Evanilson who slides in to seemingly make it three.

Woeful for United, who are saved by the offside flag.

Matheus Cunha is on for United, Tielemans off. A snub to Fernandes, perhaps. Certainly one to Tielemans.

🔄 Matheus replaced Youri during the break. https://t.co/KepOSRvVpC

Before the match kicked off, Jim White reported that United’s fans were not exactly full of cheer.

The public address announcer has just read out the teams ahead of kick off. I’m not sure in 50 years of coming to this stadium I have ever heard a United team less enthusiastically applauded. Only Harry Maguire generated what might be termed a cheer. And that was pretty lukewarm.

Bruno Fernandes has been dropped for Manchester United’s crucial Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Michael Carrick has taken the decision to drop the United captain to the bench in the wake of his public criticism on Wednesday following the shambolic 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como.

Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics and has now been taken out of the starting XI.

The move had looked likely with Carrick refusing to rule out stripping Fernandes of the captaincy when quizzed on the matter on Friday.

Carrick had responded to Fernandes questioning the set up and approach by suggesting tactics can go out of the window when players are unprepared to run.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Manchester United vs Bouremouth.

United enter Sunday’s clash against Bournemouth in the grip of a deepening crisis. Wednesday night’s dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat to debutants Como extended United’s’ winless run to seven matches across all competitions - their worst sequence since 2015.

With just one victory from their opening seven Premier League fixtures, United are enduring their worst start to a top-flight season since 1986-87. Head coach Michael Carrick, a multiple champion at Old Trafford during his playing days, finds his position under severe threat, with reports suggesting another defeat could seal his departure. While both of United’s wins this season have come at home, they remain winless in their last three at Old Trafford. On an individual level, Bryan Mbeumo has offered a rare bright spark, scoring four goals in seven league outings while Bruno Fernandes continues to search for form, and the captain’s recent outburst only makes the atmosphere more febrile.

In stark contrast, Bournemouth arrive in Manchester brimming with confidence. Marco Rose’s side have enjoyed a flawless start to their inaugural European campaign, sitting joint-top of the Europa League standings after a dominant 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s ten-man AC Milan on Thursday. That result marked a third consecutive home win and clean sheet, with Bournemouth outscoring opponents 8-0 in that stretch. Midfielder Marcus Tavernier has been instrumental, leading the club’s scoring charts with five goals across 11 appearances.

Bournemouth will feel no trepidation visiting Old Trafford, having gone unbeaten in their last six Premier League meetings with United (two wins, four draws). With Carrick desperate for a stabilising result and Rose’s side riding high on European momentum, today’s fixture carries significant stakes for both clubs.

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

Published: 14:16 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EDT, 2 November 2026

Tenerife striker Jesus de ​Miguel has been admitted to intensive care after collapsing during a Spanish second division clash with Andorra on Monday.

The 30-year-old is in stable condition, the club has confirmed, after a horrifying collision with goalkeeper ‌Jesus Owono led to the fixture being abandoned deep into stoppage time with the scores level at 2-2.

A club statement read: 'CD Tenerife player Jesús de Miguel is admitted to the ICU at the University Hospital of Nuestra Señora de Candelaria, stable despite the severity of his condition.

'The medical services at said hospital will be present and will report when there are updates.'

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

It has also been reported that while the Spaniard is stable, he remains unconscious.

Jesus de ​Miguel (pictured playing for former club Castellon) has been taken to intensive care

Tenerife's De ​Miguel was wiped out by Jesus Owono during a Spanish second tier match

The game had entered the seventh minute of stoppage time when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker appeared to be struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

The stadium has been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

Andorra also released a statement, which read: 'We want to send all our strength and best wishes to Jesus de Miguel after the serious incident suffered during today's match.

'We hope he recovers soon. A very strong hug to the player, his family and Tenerife.'

Despite remaining unconcsious in intensive care the player is believed to be 'breathing on his own'.

#1237. Vincent Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at Bayern Munich training ground

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was hospitalized after collapsing on Friday. The Belgian coach collapsed following a training session and reportedly required emergency transport. According to BILD, a rescue helicopter landed at the training ground earlier in the day. Kompany's need to go to the hospital was announced by the club on Friday afternoon.

"Vincent Kompany had to seek medical treatment on Friday after collapsing during training for FC Bayern's second team," the statement said. "The first-team coach had been watching the second team's session. Kompany will undergo thorough examination in the hospital and remain in medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage training and match operations."

Kompany also missed sessions on Monday and Tuesday ahead of the club's Champions League fixture against Arsenal, which were overseen by assistant coach Aaron Danks. The 40-year-old contracted a viral infection last week and skipped post-match interviews after Bayern's 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig, though he still managed the match from the sidelines. Danks confirmed in a pre-game news conference that the virus had affected Kompany's legs, with the manager feeling pain in them. It's not known if that same virus has any relation to Friday's collapse.

It's not the first medical emergency that Bayern have dealt with this season as midfielder Jamal Musiala had also collapsed due to microseizures related to a neurological dysfunction. During preseason, he went down off the ball after playing five minutes before needing to receive medical treatment.

Next up, Bayern Munich will face Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday. Currently undefeated to start the season, they are level atop the league table with Borussia Dortmund while sitting 14th in the Champions League standings.

While the ball retains the familiar 6-panel construction, the classic white, blue, and red colourway, and the unmistakable crown logo, itâs been upgraded with advanced features. The interior also sees improvements, with Hyperfoam cushioning now enhanced for cleaner strikes and even more power.

To mark the milestone, Mitre has launched the "The Next In Line" campaign, spotlighting the new wave of football talent carrying on their family legacies.

The campaign features rising stars such as Raphaella Wright-Phillips, granddaughter of Arsenal icon Ian Wright, Ruben Butt, son of Manchester United legend Nicky Butt, and Jacob Fowler, whose father is Liverpoolâs own Robbie Fowler.
